attributes.residual: THREE do-not-retry results, each with a root cause read from the diff. (1) damage_enemy literalization is REJECTED despite real 151 -> 143, because fuzzy regressed 99.4046 -> 98.4588 and fndiff --ops shows why: the converted form introduces a load-WIDTH divergence (target `lfs` at T[143]@0x23c where ours emits `lfd`) plus three lfd reorderings at 0x3ec/0x4c0/0x4e0. With it removed the entire residual collapses to one branch-polarity cluster (target bne/b at 0x5ac vs our beq) - that branch polarity is damage_enemy's real remaining lever, not constants. (2) The driver's apparent wins on move_logic22 (real 95 -> 49) and init_enemy (27 -> 17) DO NOT EXIST as properties of those functions: rebuilding from base with the same keep-list minus damage_enemy returned both to their exact baselines. They were downstream effects of damage_enemy's conversion reshaping the shared .sdata2 pool. Do not re-chase them. (3) The 23 score-neutral conversions were discarded rather than kept as debt removal: neutral conversions reorder the generated pool and can flip untouched byte-identical siblings from EXACT to 'MATCH (pool-name noise only)', which neither `real` nor fuzzy reports. In this TU the sampled siblings happened to show no churn rise, but the same batch pattern demonstrably did damage in critter.c, and with zero score benefit here there is nothing to pay for the risk. enemy.c should be revisited only via the branch-polarity lever on damage_enemy or the cached-alias lever the integrator flagged, not via this axis.
